newsitem.title: USA: Circus says in talks for new upscale hotel.
newsitem.headline: Circus says in talks for new upscale hotel.

text.p: Circus Circus Enterprises Inc is in talks with an unnamed operator of upscale hotels to be part of its expansion, called the "Masterplan Mile", at the south end of the Las Vegas Strip.

"Our intent is to build out the master plan as fast as possible," Circus President Glenn Schaeffer said at the Oppenheimer Gaming and Lodging conference here. "And we will do it with at least one more high-end boutique (hotel)."
Following his presentation, Schaeffer said "within a couple of months" Circus hopes to announce the partner, along with plans for the master plan's second phase, called "Project Z,".
He declined to be more specific. But the addition of a high- end hotel in one of Circus's resort/casino developments would be the second such venture for the company.

Circus currently is building the first portion of the master plan, called "Project Paradise" at a projected cost of about $850 million. That property will include two hotels, one owned and operated by Circus and a second by Four Seasons Regent Hotels and Resorts, an operator of upscale hotels.
Schaeffer said Project Paradise could be completed as soon as Christmas 1998 or the first quarter of 1999.
By quickly expanding at the south end of the strip, Circus hopes to help boost traffic to its two other hotels there, the pyramid-shaped Luxor and the castle-like Excalibur.

The Luxor recently added two new hotel room towers and completely renovated its casino. Schaeffer said the company will relaunch the Luxor to travel agents this summer with the hope of boosting traffic. He said plans call for events to take place throughout the year to boost the hotel's standing as a premiere destination in Las Vegas.

Currently occupancy at the Luxor is only in the high-80 percent range, which is below the average occupancy of 90 to 95 percent in Las Vegas. And the average room rate is in the low $80 range. Both occupancy and average room rate do not meet company expectations, Schaeffer said.
When the Luxor opened in 1993, it was one of the city's must-see hotels.
